title: Hamilton Beach Fresh Grind Electric Coffee Grinder for Beans, Spices and More, Stainless Steel Blades, Removable Chamber, Makes up to 12 Cups, Black
description:
About this item
EASY CLEANUP — DISHWASHER SAFE GRINDING BOWL: The grinding bowl on this coffee bean grinder is designed with durable stainless steel. It's removable for easy filling and pouring and is dishwasher safe..Frequency : 60 Hz
GRIND ENOUGH TO BREW UP TO 12 CUPS OF COFFEE: If you love the delicious taste of coffee made from freshly ground beans, this electric coffee grinder is perfect for the job whether you're grinding coffee for a quick cup or a full pot
SIMPLE & INTUITIVE: The coffee grinder is so easy to use that you'll want to drink flavorful coffee made from freshly ground coffee beans everyday. Just place the lid on the grinder and press the button to grind coffee. Release to stop grinding.
DURABLE STAINLESS STEEL BLADES: With the durable stainless steel blades, this grinder makes easy work of grinding everything from coffee beans to herbs and spices.
REDUCE CLUTTER WITH HIDDEN CORD STORAGE: Hideaway cord storage at the bottom of the grinder stores the cord neatly and out of sight when it's not in use. Quieter than the leading competitor

reviews_5s:
I’ve been using the Hamilton Beach Fresh Grind Electric Grinder daily for a few weeks now, and I’m genuinely impressed by how much value this compact appliance adds to my kitchen. Whether I’m grinding coffee beans for my morning brew or spices for cooking, this grinder delivers consistent, reliable results every time.

What I love:
• Quiet Operation: One of the standout features is how surprisingly quiet this grinder is compared to others I’ve owned. I can grind beans early in the morning without waking anyone up—a huge win.
• Compact Design: It doesn’t take up much counter space, and the cord wraps around the base for easy storage. It’s also light enough to tuck away in a cabinet when not in use.
• Stainless Steel Blades & Chamber: The grinding chamber is made of stainless steel and is super easy to clean. It also doesn’t hold onto smells or residue after grinding strong spices like cardamom or cloves.
• Simple One-Touch Control: There’s no learning curve—it’s intuitive and straightforward. Just press down, and you’re grinding. Hold longer for a finer grind.
• Versatility: While it’s marketed as a coffee grinder, I’ve used it successfully for seeds, spices, and even small nuts. Great for prepping fresh ingredients in seconds.

Overall, this is an incredibly useful little gadget that punches above its weight. It’s affordable, efficient, and performs reliably every day. I highly recommend it to anyone who values fresh-ground flavor and convenience in the kitchen.I'm not a coffee drinker but I do like my eggs. I purposely bought this to grind up egg shells so I can use the calcium in my garden for my tomatoes and other plants. Putting crushed egg shells in compost or in the ground takes a very, very, long time to break down to be useful. So grinding them to a powder is what works.

This grinder is great for pulverizing egg shells (after they are well dried) into powder. It only takes a couple pushes on the power button and they are finely ground. I don't know how it is with coffee beans but cleaning it is a little pain as the powder gets into the crevices of the cup area. You're probably not supposed to do this, but I give it a quick rinse under the faucet and let it completely dry before I try using it again. I probably build up enough egg shells over 2 months before I use it again anyway, so it's well dried out.I was given some coffee beans as a gift and needed a grinder. I ordered this one because of positive reviews and an affordable price. the order arrived quickly, was well packaged and damage free. I have had it for a several months now and have no issues so far. It does a great job at grinding the beans, doesn't make a mess everywhere and is easy to store when not being used.
I have been pleasantly surprised at how well it works, and because of how easy it is to use - I don't mind buy coffee beans. =0)I've been using this coffee grinder for a few months and am very pleased with it. It is far quieter than my old Krups grinder, and the design is well thought-out. The cord is quite short, but that hasn't been a problem for me. It is great being able to store the cord and also remove the grinding cup for cleaning. It quickly grinds my coffee to my satisfaction.Click to play video
I bought this to use for the raw diet I am now providing my puppy such as egg shells and pumpkin seeds that I do not want her to choke on and need to be ground finely.
I absolutely love the cord holder at the bottom. It allows you to keep this on your countertop without having a cord looking all messy. You just pop down the bottom of the unit, wrap around the cord and put the end of the plug in the notch in the back.
I did not put the lid on properly at first as you will see in the video. I made a mess but then I put it on properly. There are measurements labeled on the outside of the container so you can see how much you’re adding. I did about 2 tablespoons of roasted pumpkin seeds. At first I kept intermittent grinding, but the particles were still too big. Once I held my finger down on the button, it ground them to a powder.
I then again had issues trying to pull the container out and had to read the instructions very quickly.
Overall small learning curve just a few minutes of your time but well worth it. I also love that the containers are dishwasher safe as the blades are not removable and I do not want to cut myself while washing or shred my sponge. I put it right in the top shelf of my dishwasher and everything came out very clean.
Overall many uses besides coffee beans. Next I will try peppercorns. But please do take a moment to ensure you are putting the lid on properly and give instructions a quick read. Very easy after that!The product is easy to use and durable. Has a shorter cord but still works well despite not having a real long cord. Easy to clean grinds up beans into grounds well. Depending on how finely ground up you want the beans is basically your choice by how long you grind the beans for.I can't say enough good things about this product! I previously worked at a large chain coffee shop, so I know the importance of having a reliable grinder, and this one absolutely delivers. It effortlessly grinds hard food items down to a powder-like texture in mere seconds. Whether it’s coffee beans or any other dry ingredients, it's incredibly efficient.
I have to be honest, I bought this specifically to grind dry kibble for my 18yo dog, and it’s been a huge time-saver. The fact that I have to maintain slight pressure on the power button rather than just flipping a switch and walking away is a great feature. It ensures the process stays controlled, and I can grind the kibble to just the right texture without worry. It is also effortless to clean by lifting the small container out and rinsing it off.
Overall, this grinder has made things so much easier for me.I've had this grinder several months and love it! It's small, quiet and grinds very quickly. The basket pops out and I dump my freshly ground coffee into my coffee maker. No grounds on my kitchen counter! Perfect for 4 cups of coffee.Fast, quiet and small. Many will say you need to grind two full container batches of beans for 12-cups when the manufacturer recommends one batch. I tested, and ONE batch works for me perfectly.
More ramblings: Apparently I like a lighter brew, which I think is closer to Dunkin or our local Wawa stores. I struggled with the math of how many beans to use to make a 12 cup pot. it gets tricky as the carafe measures in 6ozs, most use 8 ozs for measuring what a coffee cup us when reality is we all use 11 or 15 oz cups. Then some online guidelines use grams and weight, or tablespoons when I have a nice 1/4 cup measuring spoon. I simply wanted a repeated process "to make full pot of coffee how many beans do I grind?" After invoking the soul of Einstein I found that it takes a LOT of coffee to make that full pot based on many online suggestions, effectively two full grind containers. you'll see many reviews here further confirming that "Have to grind twice". I'll say I am using very basic Green Mountain Breakfast Blend beans, same we used in K-cups. And the double batch recipe created a coffee that was black as the darkest night. Darker than anything I had seen in any cafe all over the US. Looked like used motor oil, and tasted VERY strong. Hmmmm. So I'll say that I did this test even tho this grinder's cup has bean fill level markings which clearly indicated 12 cups... as being one batch of grindign, not two.
I also realized my wife and I were drinking weaker coffee anyway with the K-cups. Its the same single k-cup and we are using a 15oz mug, which would be 1/2 the amount of regular grinds. The purist would say my 15oz cup requires TWO k-cups. But again with the beans I tried the recommendations of all the roasters and coffee shops... and I got motor oil looking coffee. So finally I brewed a new pot. 12 cup full pot and used ONE grind from this grinder. And the coffee was great. I dont even need a measuring spoon... just pour into the grinder cup close to the top. Done.

Just like in craft beers there are people who appreciate a high ABV dark stout beer. Me? I am a light lager guy. I am sure there are people who buy beans from all over the world and like a dark dark brew. Me? I'm a light "morning convenience store" coffee drinker

But then I wonder if this (mis)information of using so much coffee beans is put out by the industry to convince the consumer into spending so much more coffee than what the average drinker is used tu?

Long story short to save you the research and math. The experts and the math says for a standard 12-cup pot you need to run TWO full grind containers. The manufacturer says one. Try both and see what you like.

Plus my plan of just one.. 1/2 the cost of beansI needed a coffee grind, nothint ot fancy. I have found tha Hamilton beach make a quality product.
reviews_1s:
I bought this specifically because I wanted a model with a removable grinding chamber that could go in the dishwasher. Upon initial washing, a significant amount of water got stuck between the plastic and the metal of the chamber. I added a picture, but it may be difficult to tell.

This did not drain after several days of sitting and flipping. I was able to loosen the three screws on the bottom of the chamber, which seemed to help with draining, but it still took nearly two weeks for it to dry out altogether.

Considering it retained dishwater water which sat there that long, slow-leaking through the chamber, I’m not even sure how safe/sanitary it would be to use for grinding.

I contacted Hamilton-Beach customer support and after a week I got a dismissive reply that I needed to let it air out in a dry place, as if I hadn’t already explained to them that I’d tried that and it wasn’t sufficient.

Absolutely worthless, when I thought I was upgrading grinders.I had this for about six months, used regularly but not every day. Easy to use, easy to clean, fits in well with my daily routine. I make my coffee with an aeropress, and between that, getting the temperature right, and grinding from whole beans, I've been able to make the best cup of coffee I've ever had. Because I use an aeropress, the consistency of the grind isn't that big a deal, I usually just pulse or run this thing until it's all pretty fine.

The problem, though, is that if you store the power cord on this thing every time (and you should, because you shouldn't just leave your kitchen gadgets plugged in all the time), you have to pull the power cord back at a sharp angle to keep it from getting pinched by the cable storage. Over repeated use, that causes a crack in the rubber plastic that protects the wiring. This morning, though the grinder still functioned, the wire popped and sparked the second I plugged it in.

Again, this is after six months of use. Some people don't see it as a big deal to need to replace a cheap kitchen gadget at the six month mark, but for the huge fire and safety risk this is, to me that changes things.

I put in a support request with the manufacturer so I'll update when I hear back, but for the moment I absolutely recommend you look somewhere else if you don't want to die in a house fire after being electrocuted.

UPDATE: Hamilton Beach got back to me, and offered to replace my coffee grinder with a coffee grinder from either Hamilton Beach or Proctor Silex of a price NO HIGHER THAN $15.99.

That's less money than I spent on this item, and the only coffee grinder offered by either manufacturer within that price point is cheaper and worse than what I originally paid for. I told them to keep it because I just want my money back, and they refused and resent the same form letter. I said I'd take the replacement they offered, and they still haven't sent it.

I do not recommend you buy this or any other product from Hamilton Beach. If I could rate it below one star, I would.I am rating this Hamilton Beach coffee grinder as 3 only stars due to a defective product that was sent to me on my 1st order. After removing the grinder from the box, everything felt pretty solid. Then I open the cap and noticed. that the steel blade was very very loose. The blade could move up and down and wiggle a lot. The blade looks to be either riveted on or welded onto the spindle which seems to float up and down. I decided to return it and already purchased a new on which is arriving soon. The removable bowl is a very nice feature at this price. Other verified buyers responded saying that the blade should be firm and to advised to return which I did. Amazon is great at making returns and always provide excellent customer service when questions arise. Keeping my fingers crossed on a better built model to arrive. Only 3 Stars for now!

Update: I received another of the same model as I returned the first one due to a very very loose blade that moves up and down and wiggles about a 1/4 inch in any direction. The new one arrived and the box looks to be re-taped with clear packing tape on a worn smashed cornered box. After opening, everything seems new except for the same exact problem. I received the same batch of loose re-packed returned boxes that had the same problem. If this loose blade is normal for everyone, then I would look elsewhere for another brand. If this loose blade is not normal, I would approve the seller could just write these off as a lost and only sell good working ones. 1 STAR!I purchased this coffee grinder in February 2025 and it worked really well at first and then the basket that holds the coffee grounds just broke right in half one day. I also don’t use it every day so I don’t believe it’s from wear and tear. I really wanted to like this because of the removal basket that made it easy to clean.I have only used this grinder only a few times since purchase. I find it ergonomically deficient, the lid has to be aligned perfectly to seat properly. Add insult to injury the grinding blade broke off after being used easily less than 20 times. I got a lemon or it's a crap item. A stain on Hamilton Beach products.Piece of crap broke after 2 months of use. And didn't even it frequently. Probably only used <10 times over two months and the motor broke. I will NOT be buying this brand again!Very cheap. Black handle to press in order to grind fell off the first day, contacted Hamilton they said they don’t cover anything bought outside from their website so good luck. Can now hold handle on and still work it but holds very little grinds, frequently grinds spill out just opening it back up, previously had Cuisinart grinder which was much better.The absolute worst grinder I've ever used! It is very loud and doesn't grind fine at all! The coffee spills out of the grinder the entire time and makes a mess. Horrible design! Waste of money. I used it until my new one came and then threw it away. I didn't even want it as a backup.Customers should know that after 9 times using this to grind a small handful of dry dog kibble the cutter blade came off, the rubber gasket came off (in the food) and the small metal washer. My mother had one of these back in the day and it lasted from when we moved in to the house all through my teenage years. This junky thing didn't even last 2 months.
Definitely save your money and buy a more expensive one. I'm not about to contact the manufacturer to have them send me new parts!!! Just keep shopping.the portion that spins and does the grinding broke and separated from itself. It is Plastic threads holding in a screw from beneath. the threads stripped out and the pieces ended up inside of my beans. Had it 4 and a half months, cheaper quality than expected. worked fine otherwise.
